2. Facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, are that the petitioners, as plaintiff, instituted Title Suit No. 48 of 2008 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge (In-charge), Munshigonj against the opposite party Nos. 1-9, as defendant for declaration of Title and SA Khatian No. 120, RS khatian No. 141 to be declared wrong and without any legal basis stating inter alia, that the property measuring 52 decimals covered by CS and SA plot No. 601 corresponding to RS plot No. 696 of Mouza-Atigaon, originally belonged to one Rojonikanto Bhattracharya who transferred the property to one Monindra Lal Talukder by a patta. While said Monindra Lal Talukder was in possession and enjoyment of the same he transferred the schedule land to one Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick by a registered deed of sale No. 961 dated 16-3-1948. Said Yunus Mollick was in possession and enjoyment in the half share of the property measuring 26 decimals who subsequently, transferred his share by way of settlement to one Abdul Latif Bepari on 2nd Chaitra, 1355 BS Said Abdul Latif Bepari while in possession and enjoyment of the property by way of settlement from Yunus Mollick, by a registered deed No. 1775 dated 30-3-1956 transferred the suit property along with other non-suited property to Most. Ashura Khatun, Harun Or Rashid Mollick and Joynal Abedin. The said Ashura Khatun died issueless and her brother Brigadier (Rtd.) Moniruzzaman Khan succeeded her. Said Harun Or Rashid died leaving behind the plaintiff Nos. 8-13 and Joynal Abedin died leaving behind the plaintiff Nos. 1-7. While the plaintiffs went to the Tahsil office on 17-3-2008 for payment of rent for the suit property came to know that SA and RS Khatian stand recorded in the name of the predecessor of the defendants wrongly and for such wrong entry in the khatian title of the plaintiffs have become clouded, hence, the present suit for declaration. 

 6. Mr AJ Mohammad Ali, Senior Advocate with Mr Shahjada Al Amin Kabir, learned Advocates appearing for the petitioners at the very outset submit that admittedly, the suit property originally belonged to Rojonikanto Bhattacharya. CS khatian stands recorded in his name. The said Rojonikanto Bhattacharya permanently settled the suit property along with other non-suited property to one Monindra Lal Talukder by a Patta and the said Monindra Lal Talukder by a registered sale deed No. 961 dated 16-3-1948 transferred the suit property to one Yunus Mollick and another Jalal Uddin Mollick in equal share. There is no dispute between the parties regarding title of Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick. But both the courts below by making a 3rd case most unfortunately held that the parties to the suit could not satisfy the court how Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property from CS recorded owner. As such, both the courts below travelled beyond their jurisdiction in deciding title of Monindra Lal Talukder which was not a matter to be determined by the court below. 

 12. From perusal of plaint and written statement, it appears that both the parties unequivocally admitted and declared that the property in question, originally belonged to Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick by purchase vide sale deed No. 961 dated 16-3-1948. Both the courts below in finding title of Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick observed that the said two persons purchased the property from one Monindra Lal Talukder, but both the parties to the suit in their plaint and written statement failed to give any explanation or fact how Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property from CS recorded owner. I have gone through the registered deed No. 961 dated 16-3-1948 filed in original by the defendant No. 1 (exhibit-Ga) and a certified copy of the same by the plaintiff (exhibit-4) and from perusal of both the exhibits it appears that in the recital of the said deed it has been clearly mentioned that Monindra Lal Talukder acquired the property by way of permanent settlement by a registered patta dated 25 Magh 1344 corresponding to 8-2-1938. But this pertinent facts missed the notices of the trial court as well as appellate court below. 

 13. Moreover, where there is no dispute between the parties regarding acquisition of title by Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick why the trial court as well as the appellate court shall decide a question not raised before it by any party whatsoever. Therefore, this Court finds that the findings and observation of the courts below in respect of acquisition of title by Monindra, thereafter, by Yunus Mollick and Jalal Uddin Mollick is totally contrary to the actual state of affairs. The trial court as well as the appellate court in deciding title of Abdul Latif Bepari in the suit property held that the plaintiffs could not produce any document showing settlement of the property in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari by Yunus Mollick, but they could file two counterfoils of rent receipt exhibit-3 and 3ka which ought to have remained in the possession of Yunus Mollick as Zaminder and this cannot come before the court from the custody of the plaintiffs as their vendor Abdul Latif Bepari was a tenant under Yunus Mollick and also held that Abdul Latif Bepari did not acquire any title in the absence of any patta and he could not transfer the property to Most. Ashura Khatun and two others by a registered deed dated 30-3-1956 (exhibit-5). I have gone through the (exhibit-3 and 3ka), it appears that the suit property was settled by Yunus Mollick in favour of Abdul Latif Bepari on 2nd Chaitra, 1355 BS.
